To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of selected inflammatory and antioxidant genes in the group of people with depressive symptoms is associated with personality traits predisposing them to a depressive episode.

the neurotic personality traits predisposing for depressive episode are associated with the changes in peripheral gene expressions of selected indicators of inflammation (MnSod, MPO) and oxidative balance (MnSd, MMP-2, MMP9).

the scales of the Minnesota Personality Inventory-2 test (MMPI- 2) are significantly correlated with the expression at mRNA and protein level of MnSOD and MPO, as well as with the expression at protein level of metalloproteinases (MMP-9 and MMP-2) in patients diagnosed with a depressive episode.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between personality traits predisposing towards a depressive episode and the peripheral inflammatory process.
the hypothesis that depressive personality traits may be associated with the expression of inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in peripheral blood.
personality traits which may influence the expression of genes associated with inflammation and oxidative stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
personality traits predisposing towards depression are associated with an increase in peripheral expression for selected inflammatory markers.
the neurotic triads of the MMPI test correspond to the expression of Mn-SOD, MPO, and MMP-9 at the mRNA level and to the expression of MPO and MMP-9 proteins in the group of depressive patients.
the personality traits predisposing for depression are associated with the peripheral immune-inflammatory and oxidative imbalance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of Mn-SOD, MPO, MMP-2 and MMP-9 is associated with the neurotic triade of the MMPI test, and that the neurotic triode is associated with depressive personality traits.
personality traits predisposing towards a depressive episode are associated with the expression of genes responsible for inflammatory processes.
depressive patients have a tendency to be more sensitive to the inflammatory process and that their personality predisposes them to a higher level of inflammatory activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

personality traits predisposing towards depression are associated with changes at the level of peripheral gene expression, and these changes are reflected in the expression of selected inflammatory and oxidative stress indicators.
the neurotic triade of the MMPI test is associated with the expression of inflammatory and oxidative stress markers.
the expression of the genes examined is not a consequence of depression, but a predisposing factor for the development of depressive episodes.
